caveats: Every one of the 254 pilot teacher/gold disagreements (plus 4 dual-agreement corrections found during review) has now been independently adjudicated from the narrative text -- none are dropped as unadjudicated. Remaining unresolved cases are rows where the narrative genuinely supports more than one label (accept has >1 entry) or is truly unknowable from text alone (labeled UNKNOWN OR OTHER), not gaps in review.

Dual-agreement rows are, by construction, rows the Anthropic pilot model (claude-haiku-4-5) got right, which mildly favors models that behave like it. Relative ranking across models is still meaningful; treat small (<2pt) gaps with suspicion.
NHTSA CRASH/FIRE flags are carried for secondary scoring only and are known to be noisy (gotcha B1/B2).

cost_note: Cost is dominated by the ~7.4k-token system prompt resent on every row. Prompt caching already absorbs most of it; the remaining levers are batching several complaints per call, the Batch API (50% off), and trimming few-shot examples -- all of which move cost far more than switching between models in this tier.

universally_missed_rows.adjudication_note: Long history culminating in a detailed, costly transmission failure; no brake symptom appears anywhere in the (truncated) visible text. Neither original answer is supported by what's actually here.

Fire investigators themselves state the failure mechanism is undetermined -- only the general location (engine bay) is known, not a confirmed engine or electrical cause. Per the fire-routing rule, an undetermined cause goes to UNKNOWN OR OTHER. Both original answers assume a cause the text doesn't confirm.
ABS malfunction with a replaced wheel-speed sensor -- an ABS/hydraulic-brake component, no stability/skid symptom described. Gold is right.

Paint peeling (cosmetic/finish issue, explicitly the complainant's stated main concern) is not really a STRUCTURE (frame/chassis integrity) issue -- teacher overreached into a poor-fit specific category instead of using UNKNOWN OR OTHER, which gold correctly did.
ABS malfunction on a passenger Buick, dealer confirmed normal (non-ABS) brakes were fine -- no air-brake indication. Gold is right.

Repeated stalling with power-steering/brake loss as a downstream consequence; the dealer explicitly found nothing and no component is named. Same reasoning as 2016886. Neither original answer is confirmed.
Dashboard (interior) lights going out, not exterior headlights/taillights -- the rare INTERIOR LIGHTING category is the precise fit that neither original answer used.
Spontaneous sunroof glass shattering while closed -- matches the established convention that sunroof-glass failures are VISIBILITY, not structural. Gold is right.

Explicitly cites Honda Service Bulletin 16-008, a documented transmission-control-module 'creep forward' surge defect -- a named, specific root cause pointing to the drivetrain, not a brake malfunction. Gold is right.

Dashboard surface degrading/melting is a material/cosmetic defect, not a structural-integrity failure (same reasoning as the paint-peeling case above). The 'Takata recall' mention appears to be the complainant's own confusion, unrelated to the actual described issue. Gold is right.

'All power will turn off' with no named component (no wiring/battery/fuse/ignition mentioned) -- fits our own UNKNOWN OR OTHER definition exactly. Gold is right, teacher overreached to ELECTRICAL SYSTEM without a named part.
Narrative describes the car being 'hacked' via 'wave frequency' -- not a coherent technical fault description of any real vehicle system.
Text explicitly names 'a dangerous faulty hydraulic control unit (and ABS system)' -- confirms the hydraulic subtype directly, no air-brake evidence on this pickup.
'Engine Power Reduced' mode causing inability to accelerate at highway speed is functionally the same throttle-response-loss pattern as 928059 and 2026794. Neither original answer is right.
Purely cosmetic paint peeling, not a structural-integrity failure -- STRUCTURE overreaches here. Gold is right.
Textbook accelerator-pedal-response delay. Gold is right, teacher's off-list answer is wrong.
Dealer's actual repair recommendation explicitly named a thermostat replacement (a cooling-system part). Gold is right, teacher too conservative given a specific repair was named.

universally_missed_note: Every evaluated model disagreed with the gold set on these rows. Where the models unanimously agree on the same alternative label, the gold set (or the underlying adjudication) is the more likely error and should be re-read.
